summary: Four findings: two false standalone statements need a unit restriction or a nonzero-module branch; the explicit §2.1 measure constructions lack extraction items; a confirmed Euler-sum correction was not propagated. No new roadmap or second proof owner is proposed. Source-error claims are scoped to arXiv v2 and the inspected author copy, not the inaccessible version of record.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22.result.json — item /17, finite–singular comparison (3.1); proposed owners EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems:ES.1 and HeegnerPointEulerSystems:HE.5
findings.claim: The standalone comparison with G_ℓ = Gal(K[ℓ]/K[1]) is false without a restriction on the image of the units of O_K. Item /17 permits K=Q(sqrt(-3)), p=3, ℓ=2, R=Z_3 and the trivial representation T=Z_3. Then I_2=(3), H¹_f(K_λ,F_3)=F_3, but G_2=0 and hence H¹_s(K_λ,F_3)⊗G_2=0. This concerns the reusable generic definition, not the main Eisenstein theorems in their more restrictive setting.
findings.evidence: arXiv:2008.02571v2, §3.1, p.16, (3.1), https://arxiv.org/pdf/2008.02571v2: “there is a finite-singular comparison isomorphism”. Read the full paragraph and its page image; the author copy https://web.math.ucsb.edu/~castella/Eisenstein.pdf has the same assertion. The preceding Artin-symbol identification omits the unit quotient. Explicit check: X²+X+1 is irreducible modulo 2; the image of ζ_3 generates (O_K/2)×=F_4×, so quotienting by global units kills the whole residue group. Equivalently, the only reduced primitive positive binary forms of discriminants -3 and -12 are (1,1,1) and (1,0,3), respectively: both ring class groups are trivial. Continuous unramified homomorphisms from the procyclic residue Galois group to F_3 give the nonzero left side. E1–E41 do not record this restriction.
findings.fix: Correct the finite–singular component of /17 to assume p does not divide [O_K×:O_ℓ×] for each auxiliary ℓ, or use the sufficient uniform condition p∤#O_K×. Keep the general Selmer-structure definition separate from this additional hypothesis. Record the missing hypothesis as a sourceIssue scoped to arXiv v2 and the inspected author copy, with sourceVersions; do not assert an uninspected journal error. Explain that the odd-p, p∤D_K setting of §3.2 discharges this restriction. Preserve ES.1 as the abstract owner and HE.5 as its arithmetic consumer; no new roadmap is needed.

findings.claim: The asserted choice of a cyclic summand to omit requires M≠0. The item includes M=M′=X=0, k=1, a=a′=b=b′=0. Both required exact sequences are the identity on R/𝔪, and k>exp(M)+2a and a′≤a hold. But s=0, so there is no index 1≤i_0≤2s. The source and extraction need an explicit nonzero branch.
findings.evidence: arXiv:2008.02571v2, §3.3.2, pp.22–23, (3.11)–(3.13) and Proposition 3.3.11(i): “There exists 1≤i_0≤2s”. The same quantifier is visible on p.23 of the inspected author copy. The definition exp(M)=min{n≥0:π^nM=0} on p.22 gives exp(0)=0. Substitution of the displayed witness leaves 0→0→R/𝔪→R/𝔪→0 in each row, with α and β identity. The proof in §3.3.3 separately disposes of s=0 before its induction, so this is a defect in the exported general algebra lemma, not a counterexample to Theorem 3.2.1. E28 concerns a different part of Proposition 3.3.11.
findings.fix: Split the statement: for s>0, retain the existing omitted-summand assertion with i_0∈{1,…,2s}; for s=0, use the canonical injection 0→X without choosing an index. Keep the other conclusions with their appropriate index ranges. Add a sourceIssue and version record for the unqualified quantified statement, and state in the report why the application already lies in the nonzero branch.

findings.where: research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22.result.json — items /13 and /15; §2.1 construction coverage and statuses
findings.claim: Item /13 gives the interpolation theorem and a narrative mention of its construction, but the extraction gives no item with a defining statement/status for the actual local Serre–Tate measure μ_(f,a), the Atkin–Serre operator and p-depletion, or the p-depleted measure with support on Z_p×. These are constructions explicitly recalled and used by this paper to pass from congruent modular forms to congruent measures. They are not recursive proof closure of an external theorem.
findings.evidence: arXiv:2008.02571v2, proof of Theorem 2.1.1, pp.12–13, especially (2.2)–(2.3): the text defines μ_(f,a) by its binomial moments, defines θ and f^flat, and then forms the measure on units used in the class-group sum. Searches and reading of all 39 items found only the closing narrative in /13 and the congruence explanation in /15. At Mathlib 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174, Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/MahlerBasis.lean:339,357 proves PadicInt.hasSum_mahler and mahlerEquiv for complete ultrametric coefficient modules; Measure/AmiceTransform.lean:75,91,156 defines the coefficient-general transform, proves its injectivity, but provides amiceTransformEquiv only for Z_p-valued measures. Thus the coefficient-general source construction is not simply an already-built inverse equivalence. Reviewed AUDIT-26 for PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2 and AUDIT-25 for GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.9 record the corresponding distinction. The existing PadicMeasures packet already plans L2/bounded-inverse-amice and unit restriction.
findings.fix: Add separate extraction items for (a) V_p(N;R), its Serre–Tate expansion at the specified CM point and θ with its q-expansion action; (b) μ_(f,a) characterized by ∫binom(x,m)dμ=binom(θ,m)f(x_a), including the coefficient ring; and (c) p-depletion and the resulting unit-supported measure. Give the p-adic modular-form input its existing PadicFamilies:L0 / AutomorphicPadicLFunctions:L3 ownership and the BDP-specific constructions GrossZagierAndArithmeticHeights:GZ.9 ownership. Import the bounded-coefficient inverse Amice and restriction operations from PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras:L2; cite the pinned Mathlib Mahler substrate rather than re-plan it. If any required source-specific comparison is marked missing, route it once into the appropriate existing proposed layer. Do not create another Igusa or measure roadmap: RS-14 retains source-specific mixed-characteristic comparisons after importing IG.1’s precise special-fiber scope. No APIs, unit tests or reconstruction of the cited papers’ proofs are required for this extraction fix.

findings.claim: The accepted extraction records the archimedean-index mistake in E18 but still uses its uncorrected formula in item /11. It sums λ(P_w(θ)) over w∈Σ, w∤p, although Σ contains ∞ and that Euler polynomial has not been defined at infinity. The actual exported sum must run over the finite imprimitive set S.
findings.evidence: Internal evidence: /E18 has review.verdict=confirmed by REV-PAPER-CASTELLA-ETAL-22 and explicitly corrects this index set to S=Σ∖{v,v̄,∞}. Item /11 still contains the old index set. This agrees with arXiv v2, §1.2, (1.6), Proposition 1.2.5 and its proof, pp.8–9: the local exact sequence is indexed by S. The extraction’s item /16 already uses S correctly. PROTOCOL §18 requires items to contain the corrected statement.
findings.fix: Replace the sum in item /11 by Σ_(w∈S) λ(P_w(θ)), define S=Σ∖{v,v̄,∞} there or by a precise reference, and cite E18 in the note. Keep the existing confirmed sourceIssue rather than duplicating it. Update the human report’s correction list so this propagated repair is visible.
